items.evidence: The reload step (diff lines 133-140) checks the rules placeholder is visible and the rule count is 0 after page.reload(). That would fail if the promotionRuleDelete mutation never ran.
Both acceptance criteria are asserted. No rules right after confirming: lines 126-127. After a reload, still no rules and the name is still 'E2E Tee sale' in the header and name input: lines 134-139.

No existing page object covers promotions, and none of the new locators (search-input, list, datagrid-row-anchor, page-header) appear anywhere in e2e/. PROMOTIONS and PRODUCTS are reused from the scenario.
No waitForTimeout, sleeps or polling loops. It waits on URLs, attributes and dialog state.
test and expect come from ../../fixtures/test.ts (line 91). The test is not tagged parallel() and writes nothing to the cache or dumps.
It uses getByTestId and a role locator. The rule delete button is scoped to the rule card. The coordinate hover is a documented workaround for Glide's canvas rows, which have no locatable element.
It uses the existing ORDERS_SCENARIO promotion as-is, with no API or UI set-up.
No hard-coded ids: the detail URL is matched with a regex. Expected values come from PROMOTIONS.catalogue and PRODUCTS.tee.
The admin actor is set through test.use (line 104). There is no UI sign-in, and the ticket gives no specific permission.
typecheck.txt reports exit 0. The spec is at e2e/tests/discounts/promotion-rule-removal.spec.ts.
Line 119 (spec): the locator rule.getByTestId("rule-value-chip") is written inline in the spec instead of on PromotionPage.
All page-object members are readonly fields initialised from this.page, and both classes use constructor(readonly page: Page) {}.
It has // Arrange and // Act & Assert (lines 107, 113).
One test with a named test.step for each stage (lines 114, 124, 133).
The title 'Staff removes a rule from a promotion #e2e #discounts' describes the behaviour and has the #e2e tag.
The header comment (lines 95-103) says what the spec covers and which legacy case it replaces.
All assertions are web-first. boundingBox() is only used to position the hover, not in an assertion.
It uses ORDERS_SCENARIO, PROMOTIONS.catalogue.name and percent, and PRODUCTS.tee.name, with no typed-in expected values.
No cleanup code and no unique names.
No per-test timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep the .ts extension. The page object takes expect from @playwright/test, as draftOrderPage.ts and homePage.ts already do, and the spec takes it only from the fixture.
No any, casts or gql calls.
The comments explain why: the canvas hover, the save-bar Delete pitfall, and checking the placeholder before the count because of the loading skeleton.

structured_output.summary: I judged all 23 items: 22 met and 1 failed. The change is solid. The rule removal is proven by checks made after a reload, both acceptance criteria are covered, the new PromotionPage covers a screen nothing else in the suite does, and the type check passes. The one finding is minor: M1, because line 119 of the spec writes the rule-value-chip locator inline instead of putting it on the page object. Nothing was run, as instructed.
